The stone corridors of {{Basgiath War College|loc}} hum with the low, sullen murmur of tired bodies and the clatter of studded leather armor. 

Every footstep on the damp flagstones sends a dull ache vibrating up {{Violet Sorrengail|npc}}'s ankles, a sharp reminder of the fragile joints she works so hard to keep in place. 

She rubs her right wrist where the protective leather binding chafes against the skin, her mind still snagged on {{Mira Sorrengail|npc}}'s parting warning about trusting no one—especially not the ones who think they know what's best for her.

The heavy oak doors of the mess hall stand ajar, spilling out a suffocating wave of roasted meat, stale sweat, and the sharp edge of circulating tension. 

Inside, long wooden tables groan under the weight of hungry first-years and predatory upperclassmen sizing up the new meat. 

Violet scans the crowded benches, her gaze darting past the black uniforms of the unbonded and the deep scarlet of the second-years, looking for a familiar face that won't immediately translate to a knife between the ribs.

"Violet." 

The voice is clipped, authoritative, and instantly recognizable before a hand clamps down with familiar rigidity on her shoulder. 

It is {{Dain Aetos|id: dain_aetos}}, his second-year chevron gleaming on his collar, his expression a tight mask of professional disapproval and personal anxiety. 

"You shouldn't even be walking this corridor alone," Dain says, his eyes dropping briefly to her bound wrists before snapping back to her face with an intensity that borders on a reprimand. 

"The second-years are already taking bets on who survives the first week of sparring. You need to sit at the squad table where I can watch your flank."

The stone corridors of {{Basgiath War College|loc}} hum with the low, bruising friction of hundreds of cadets shifting between the grueling trials of the {{Riders Quadrant|faction}} and whatever meager rest could be scavenged. Every footstep echoes off the damp masonry, carrying the metallic tang of dried blood and sweat that never quite washes out of the stone. 

Violet walks with a measured, deliberate gait, keeping her weight balanced to spare her notoriously fragile joints while her mind loops endlessly over {{Mira Sorrengail|npc}}'s sharp warning at the parapet. Her fingers graze the edge of her leather-bound notebook tucked safely beneath her arm, a comforting anchor of ink and history in a place where iron and teeth ruled. 

The heavy oak doors of the mess hall groan open, spilling a wall of chaotic noise, roasted meat, and damp wool into the corridor. Long trestle tables groan under the weight of pewter flagons and plates of salted bread, packed densely with first-years nursing fresh bruises and older cadets swapping dark jokes about the upcoming threshing. 

Before Violet can scan the room for a neutral face, a heavy hand clamps firmly onto her shoulder—too firmly, sending an instant, sharp twinge of pain through her vulnerable left clavicle. She stifles a sharp intake of breath, turning to find {{Dain Aetos|npc}} standing there in his crisp second-year leather, his expression carved from absolute, unyielding worry.

"You shouldn't be wandering around alone, Violet," Dain says, his voice dropping into that familiar, suffocating register of absolute authority that always made her feel like she was back in the archives at the age of ten. "Come on. I saved a seat at our squad table where nobody will bother you."

'I don't need a babysitter, Dain,' she thinks, jaw tightening as she feels every eye in her immediate vicinity flick toward them, measuring her stature, her pale hair, and the undeniable protection of a second-year squad leader.

My fingers close tightly around the canvas strap of my satchel, hoisting the heavy leather bag over my shoulder with a familiar, dull ache radiating through my left collarbone. Mira's parting warning still echoes in the hollow chambers of my mind, buzzing beneath the surface like trapped hornets. *'Trust no one. Especially not Xaden.'* Every muscle in my body feels strung to the point of snapping after the brutal, lung-burning nightmare of crossing the parapet, but there is no time to nurse bruises or catch my breath in this stone-hewn crucible of death.

I step out into the damp, salt-scented chill of the courtyard, keeping my head low and my gaze fixed on the uneven cobblestones beneath my boots. The morning air carries the sharp scent of singed wool and horse sweat from the lower stables, mingling with the heavy iron tang of tension that permanently stains Basgiath War College. I steer wide of the central training ring, silently calculating the fastest, most shadowed route toward the mess hall where I might find a moment of quiet anonymity to steady my rattled nerves.

'Just blend in,' I tell myself, swallowing hard against the dry, metallic taste of panic as I skirt the edge of the massive stone barracks. 'Keep moving, don't draw eyes, and for the love of everything holy, do not cross paths with the shadow-wielding wingleader whose executioner's gaze is probably already burning a hole in my back.'

The heavy timber doors of the mess hall loom ahead, leaking the raucous, chaotic noise of hundreds of starving, adrenaline-fueled cadets devouring their morning rations. As I reach for the heavy iron ring of the handle, a firm, familiar hand suddenly catches my right elbow, gripping with an agonizingly protective pressure that instantly threatens to wrench my shoulder from its socket.

"Violet," {{Dain Aetos|npc}}’s voice drops low, taut with the familiar, suffocating blend of childhood affection and absolute military rigidity that has dictated half my life. "You shouldn't be walking alone across the quadrangle. Especially not with the target your mother painted on your back."

My fingers close tightly around the stiff leather strap of my satchel, hoisting the heavy bag over my shoulder with a sharp ache that radiates straight down my collarbone.
Mira's parting words still echo through my mind, a chilling reminder of the blood on these stone floors and the sheer impossibility of surviving a quadrant where my own mother wanted me dead.
I keep my head down, navigating the damp, torch-lit corridors of Basgiath War College toward the mess hall, my eyes scanning the shadows for that familiar, lethal silhouette of midnight-dark hair and scarred obsidian eyes.
I cannot afford another run-in with {{Xaden Riorson|npc}}, not when my pulse is still hammering a frantic rhythm against my ribs and my joints feel dangerously loose beneath my protective leather bindings.

The heavy oak doors of the mess hall groan open as I push through them, the dense wall of noise, roasted meat, and damp wool washing over me.
Cadets crowd the long wooden tables, shouting over one another, laughing, and nursing fresh bruises from morning drills.
I slip along the periphery, hugging the rough stone wall to avoid the press of armored bodies that could easily dislocate a shoulder with a careless shove.
'Just keep moving, find a corner, and block out the noise,' I tell myself, my breath coming in short, controlled pulls as I search the room for a quiet bench.

"Violet."

The voice is entirely too familiar, carrying that clipped, authoritative cadence that belongs solely to a second-year squad leader who thinks he owns the world—or at least thinks he owns me.
I stiffen, turning slowly to find {{Dain Aetos|npc}} stepping out from the shadow of a stone archway, his uniform impeccably maintained, his jaw set in that familiar, immovable line of absolute disapproval.
He doesn't waste time on pleasantries; his gaze immediately drops to my hands, scanning my wrists for any sign of the tremors or instability he expects from me.

"You shouldn't be walking alone across the quadrant, especially not after what happened on the Parapet," Dain says, his steps closing the distance between us with an irritatingly protective deliberation.
His hand reaches out, fingers curling firmly around my forearm to steady me—an instinctive gesture of childhood friendship that feels less like comfort and more like an iron shackle.
"I told you I'd keep you alive, Vi, but you're making it entirely too difficult by trying to disappear into the crowd."

twist: Dain intercepts me right outside the dorm door rather than letting me reach the mess hall alone, intensifying his overprotective suffocating oversight.

My fingers close tightly around the worn leather strap of my satchel, the weight of my father's journals pressing reassuringly against my ribs even as my joints throb with a dull, familiar ache. Mira's parting words still echo in the hollows of my mind, a sharp warning about who to trust and who to watch out for—advice I desperately need to heed if I intend to survive this godforsaken war college. 

I step out into the damp, chill air of the corridor, keeping my head down and my breathing shallow. Every step on the stone floor requires conscious calculation, my ankles protesting the abrupt shift in weight as I navigate the drafty stone archways toward the mess hall, my eyes darting down every intersecting hallway in a silent prayer that I won't cross paths with the shadow-wielding, dark-eyed wingleader whose gaze still burns behind my eyelids.

'Just keep moving, don't draw attention, and for God's sake, don't let anyone see how badly your knees are shaking.'

The heavy scent of scorched fat, stale ale, and damp wool grows thicker as I approach the vaulted stone hall where hundreds of exhausted, bloodied cadets are already tearing at their morning rations. Before I can slip through the massive iron-strapped double doors, a heavy hand clamps down on my shoulder, making me flinch and nearly sending my left hip out of its socket with a sharp, sickening pop.

"Violet," {{Dain Aetos|npc}}'s voice cuts through the din, dropping with that familiar, maddening blend of authority and condescension that makes my teeth grind. He steps into my line of sight, his second-year leather armor stiff and immaculate, his blue eyes scanning my face with intense, bureaucratic scrutiny. "You shouldn't be walking alone, especially not after what happened on the Parapet. The squad leaders are already taking bets on who survives the first week, and I won't have you making yourself a target."

I suppress a grimace, shifting my weight to ease the pressure on my hip while keeping my expression carefully neutral. "I am perfectly capable of walking to breakfast on my own, Dain, without an escort keeping score," I murmur, my voice low and laced with a quiet, stubborn defiance that never seems to get through to him.

Dain's jaw tightens, his hand lingering on my shoulder with a possessive firmness that feels less like friendship and more like a leash. 'He still thinks I'm the fragile little girl sitting in the Scribe archives, waiting for him to protect me from the real world.'

Around us, other cadets shove past, laughing loudly, covered in fresh bruises and dirt from early morning drills, paying us no mind as the brutal reality of Basgiath continues its relentless march.

twist: The dagger's dark, unfamiliar weight reacts strangely to the ambient magic of Basgiath's wards, creating a faint, localized hum that catches Dain's sharp, suspicious eye rather than staying entirely unnoticed.

The cold iron of the floor presses through Violet's boots as she reaches deep into the inner lining of her cadet tunic, her fingers wrapping around the hilt of a weapon that does not belong in the halls of [[Basgiath War College|loc]]. 

It is a [[Venin-Forged Dagger|item]], an obsidian-dark blade shaped with jagged, unsettling angles that drink the torchlight rather than reflecting it. Forged by the very hands of the enemy she has only read about in contraband manuscripts, its edge carries a dark resonance—a lethal beauty capable of piercing even the thickest dragon scale. 

Her father left it among his private journals, a secret kept hidden from the harsh gaze of [[General Lilith Sorrengail|npc]] and the watchful eyes of the [[Navarre Military Leadership|faction]]. 

Across the damp stone chamber, {{Dain Aetos|npc}} stiffens, his gaze snapping from the drill roster to the subtle shift in Violet's posture. "What are you doing, Violet?" Dain asks, his voice dropping to a harsh, controlled murmur as he takes a sharp step closer, his hand instinctively hovering near the pommel of his own standard-issue blade. 'If anyone else sees that, we're both dead.'

Dain's fingers twitch at his side, torn between his duty to report every contraband item in the quadrant and his desperate desire to shield her from her own recklessness. 

"Put it away," he whispers, his jaw tight, his chest rising and falling in a sharp, agitated rhythm as he scans the shadows of the corridor for approaching cadets. "You have no idea what you're holding, or who would kill you just to possess it."

<nar>
The stone of {{The Parapet|loc}} narrows to a jagged tooth of slate, slick with morning mist and devoid of the iron handrails that once flanked the outer edge. Below, the stone walls of the {{Riders Quadrant|faction}} drop away into a sheer, stomach-churning abyss where the clouds drift lazily against the sheer cliff face. 

Violet doesn't hesitate. Every second wasted is another step toward the iron gates swinging shut, locking her out of the quad before her conscription is even officially logged. 

Her boots strike the damp stone with a sharp, echoing snap, her arms held wide to balance her slight frame against the biting mountain draft. 

'Keep the center of gravity low. Trust the bindings,' she tells herself, her breath frosting in the thin air as she forces her legs to move with mechanical precision. 

Halfway across the span, the ancient masonry shudders. A chunk of weathered shale breaks away beneath her left heel, plummeting silently into the fog below as her ankle violently twists inward with a sickening pop of a shifting joint. 

Pain shoots white-hot up her calf, threatening to buckle her knees and send her pitching over the side. 

Teeth gritted so hard her jaw aches, Violet drops instantly to her hands and knees, ignoring the agonizing scrape of skin against rough stone. 

She crawls forward with desperate, clawing urgency, using her upper body strength to drag her weight across the remaining treacherous meters of the span. 

Up ahead, {{Dain Aetos|npc}} freezes in his tracks near the broader stone landing, his structured posture snapping into absolute rigidity as he catches sight of her method of crossing. 

"Violet! What in the name of the gods are you doing?" Dain shouts across the gap, his voice cracking with a mixture of disbelief and frantic, protective anger. 

He takes two steps back onto the narrow stone as if to intercept her, his hands hovering uselessly at his sides because the ledge is too narrow for two. 

"You're going to get yourself killed! Get off the edge right now!" he barks, his eyes wide with the stark terror of a rule-abiding soldier watching someone deliberately shatter every safety protocol in existence. 

Violet pays him no mind, lunging the final yard onto the solid flagstones of the inner courtyard and collapsing against the cold fortress wall, her chest heaving as she fights the wave of nausea from the dislocated joint. 

The heavy iron gates groan on their massive hinges just behind Dain, beginning their slow, inevitable swing toward closure. 

Dain reaches down, grabbing her by the upper arm with a bruising, rigid grip to haul her upright, his jaw tight and his gaze sharp with reprimand. 

"You're reckless," Dain mutters, his breath hot and ragged against her ear as he pulls her past the threshold just as the gates slam shut with a thunderous finality. 
</nar>

<nar>
The noise of the mess hall hits me like a physical blow—the clatter of heavy pewter plates, the raucous laughter of second and third-year cadets trading boasts of survival, and the underlying, electric tension of those of us marked with the yellow stripe of first-years. My joints ache from the endless hours of standing and the treacherous crossing of {{The Parapet|loc}}, every step a quiet negotiation with my own fragile connective tissue. 

Then I spot her across the crowded, grease-stained wooden tables. 

{{Mira Sorrengail|npc}} sits amidst a cluster of veteran riders, her leather armor scuffed and scarred from active duty, dark hair pulled back in a practical braid that brooks no nonsense. Even surrounded by towering cadets twice her physical bulk, she commands the space with an effortless, lethal authority that reminds me terrifyingly of our mother, {{General Lilith Sorrengail|npc}}. 

I weave through the press of bodies, my fingers instinctively checking the protective leather wrappings around my wrists and ankles. 

As I approach, {{Dain Aetos|npc}} steps smoothly into my path, his hand resting on the pommel of his standard-issue blade with all the rigid, self-righteous certainty of a second-year squad leader who thinks he can coddle me through a war college. 

"Violet, you shouldn't be wandering the mess hall alone," Dain murmurs, his brow furrowing with that familiar, suffocating protectiveness that treats me like a glass doll about to shatter. "The upper-classmen from the quadrant sections aren't looking at you as a cadet. They're looking at you as General Sorrengail's weak spot."

'I am not a glass doll, Dain, and I need to speak to my sister,' I think, biting back the sharp retort that rests on the tip of my tongue because making an enemy of my designated protector on day one is a tactical error I cannot afford. 

"I need to talk to Mira, Dain," I say aloud, keeping my voice steady despite the way my pulse hammers against my ribs. 

Dain opens his mouth to object further, but Mira’s voice cuts through the din like a drawn stiletto. 

"Let her through, Aetos. She's a cadet now, or have you forgotten how to follow a superior's order?" Mira doesn't stand up, but her sharp gaze locks onto mine, cold and calculating. 

Dain stiffens, his jaw tightening before he reluctantly steps aside, casting a wary glance between the two of us as I slide onto the bench across from my sister. 

Mira leans forward across the scarred wood, her dark eyes scanning my face with an intensity that misses nothing—not the slight tremor in my fingers, nor the pale strain around my mouth. 

"You look terrible, Vi," Mira says, her tone stripped of any sisterly softness, raw with a desperate, hidden fear she rarely lets anyone see. "And before you start complaining about the muscle cramps or the weight of the packs, tell me why you're looking at me like you're already writing your own obituary."

"I'm worried about what's coming, Mira," I admit, the confession dragging out of me against my better judgment as I lean closer, lowering my voice beneath the roar of the mess hall. "Everyone here expects me to die on the mat or burn on the flight field before the month is out. Mother didn't put me here to survive—she put me here to quietly disappear where the scribes couldn't protect me. I need to know what I'm actually facing, because the official orientation is a lie."

Mira's expression hardens into something terrifyingly grim, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she glances around the hall to ensure no one is listening in on our corner. 

"You're right to be terrified, Vi," Mira whispers fiercely, reaching across the table to grip my wrist with fingers like iron bands, her thumb pressing directly over my sensitive pulse point. "Mother didn't send you here to graduate. She sent you here because she thinks the Scribe Quadrant is too vulnerable to whatever is leaking across the borders, or she simply stopped caring if you survived the culling. Listen to me very carefully: nobody cares about your bones or your dislocations out here. If you want to see tomorrow, you stop relying on Dain's archaic rules and you learn how to use your brain as a weapon before someone uses it as a stepping stone."
</nar>
